items.prompt: A v2 PATCH body is {"marketingOptIn": false}. What canonical patch does the adapter produce?
items.answer: { marketingOptIn: false } and no other keys
distractors: {} with no keys, as false counts as not provided
{ marketingOptIn: undefined } and no other keys
{ marketingOptIn: false, lifecycleState: 'ACTIVE' }
items.explanation: The adapter builds a fresh object and assigns a key only when the payload value is !== undefined, so an explicit false survives and omitted fields stay absent.

items.prompt: Prisma skips undefined values on update anyway. Why does the guide still object to padding every optional key with undefined?
items.answer: Object.keys would list each padded field, so the audit's changedFields lies
distractors: Prisma actually writes NULL for undefined keys on an update call
JSON.stringify throws on undefined keys when the audit is logged
Undefined keys make the Zod schema reject the patch as malformed
items.explanation: The audit record uses changedFields: Object.keys(input); a padded object makes the audit trail claim every field changed.

items.prompt: A v1 client PATCHes only {"email": "a@b.co"}. Which keys does the canonical patch contain?
items.answer: Only email: givenName/familyName are added only when fullName was present
distractors: email, givenName, familyName: the names are copied from the stored profile
email and familyName: v1 sets familyName to 'Unknown' when it is missing
email and lifecycleState: v1 status defaults to active on every patch
items.explanation: migrated is undefined when fullName is absent, so no name keys are assigned.

items.prompt: A v1 client creates a profile with fullName "Cher". What does a v2 client later read as the name?
distractors: givenName 'Cher', familyName '' (empty)
givenName '', familyName 'Cher'
a 400 error, as v1 needs two name parts
items.explanation: splitFullName joins the remaining parts or falls back to 'Unknown'; v1 compatibility is intentionally lossy.

items.prompt: A profile is in TRIAL. A v1 client reads it and writes its status straight back unchanged. What is the stored lifecycle afterwards?
items.answer: ACTIVE: TRIAL reads as 'active', and 'active' maps back to ACTIVE
distractors: TRIAL: unchanged values are skipped, so nothing is written
SUSPENDED: TRIAL is mapped to inactive on the way back
409: the lifecycle change from TRIAL is rejected as invalid
items.explanation: toLegacyStatus presents ACTIVE and TRIAL as active; fromLegacyStatus maps active to ACTIVE. The round-trip silently ends the trial (senior finding 5).

items.prompt: Where should the owner of a newly created profile come from?
items.answer: The trusted session, never the request body
distractors: The request body's ownerId, once Zod validates it
The x-api-version header sent with the request
The body if present, and only otherwise the session
items.explanation: The route passes apiContext.session.userId into toCanonicalCreateInput; the service must also refuse a foreign owner from direct callers.

items.prompt: A client sends x-api-version: v9. Why does it get a framework 500 instead of a 400?
items.answer: The catch block calls getRequestedVersion again, which throws outside any try
distractors: The registry has no v9 entry, so a TypeError escapes before the try starts
The route deliberately maps unknown versions to 500 so operators get alerted
Zod rejects the header and Next.js converts every ZodError into a 500
items.explanation: An error handler that re-runs the failing operation turns a clean 400 into an uncaught error.

items.prompt: After a successful create, recordVersionUsage throws because the metrics store is down. What does the client experience, and what is the knock-on risk?
items.answer: An error despite the saved profile; a retry may duplicate it
distractors: A 201; usage recording runs after the response has been sent
A 201 with a warning header; the failure is logged for operators
An error; the profile write is rolled back with the metrics call
items.explanation: Usage recording is awaited on the success path before returning, coupling a non-critical side effect to the client's outcome.

items.prompt: Why is the version rollout gate trivially bypassable?
items.answer: The bucket hashes a caller-chosen clientId header
distractors: The bucket uses Math.random, so a retry lands inside
The allowlist matches client ids with startsWith
Percentages above 100 silently disable the check
items.explanation: stableBucket sums clientId character codes mod 100 and clientId comes from a request header, so a caller picks a clientId whose sum lands under the percentage; the hash is also poorly distributed.

items.prompt: The services enforce role and ownership checks carefully. Why does the review still call every authorization rule 'advisory' in this demo?
items.answer: Identity and role come from headers, so anyone can claim ADMIN
distractors: The checks run after the repository write, so they block nothing
Roles are cached per process, so a revoked admin stays an admin
The services skip their checks whenever NODE_ENV is development
items.explanation: requireSession trusts x-user-id / x-user-role / x-client-id; a signed session must replace this adapter.

items.prompt: In updateProfile, what is the order of guards, repository write and audit record?
items.answer: All guards, then repository.update, then the audit record
distractors: The audit first, so every attempted change is logged
repository.update first, then guards on the stored result
Guards and update first, then lifecycle checks after the write
items.explanation: 'Validate before each side effect': a rejected operation must leave rows and audit entries unchanged.

items.prompt: A client sends no x-api-version header. Which contract does it get, and why is that a problem?
items.answer: v1, the deprecated contract, because it is still marked isDefault
distractors: v2, because the newest registered version is the default
A 400, because the header is mandatory for every request
Whichever version the client's rollout bucket happens to select
items.explanation: The registry marks v1 isDefault: true while its lifecycle is DEPRECATED.

items.front: Which layer owns what in the ww27 profile API?
items.back: Adapter: translate version names/statuses into one canonical model. Service: ownership, role, lifecycle and no-op policy (so direct callers get the same protections). Repository: session read scope. Audit metadata: after a successful repository operation.

items.front: Presence is a data contract: omitted vs false vs empty
items.back: Omitted means leave the stored value alone; false, zero or an empty array are deliberate values. Validation rejects only what the contract declares invalid, and the adapter never invents values for omitted fields, so patches are assembled field by field.

items.front: Why must an unknown API version fail rather than fall back?
items.back: It is a routing error, not a request to serve silently with defaults. Explicit errors are easier to monitor and safer for clients; route params and JSON are untrusted strings even when the parameter is typed ApiVersionId, so check at runtime before any write.

items.front: What do fake repositories prove about profile + audit persistence?
items.back: Call ordering only, not cross-connection atomicity. The profile and audit writes are sequential; document that limit and require a transaction-capable repository before claiming stronger guarantees.
